title: Schedule v1
description: POST /v1/schedule and the engine bridge's engine.schedule (specs/step-w/SPEC-W2.md points 5 and 22, gap map G32). The Loop module plans its timers, reminders, check-ins and calendar entries, and the engine dates them: each request names a base date (an engine item, a date the person typed, or today) and an offset (calendar days, business days, months, or a product setting), and the engine gives back the date and its days_away. The screen never adds or counts days itself. Stateless: nothing is stored and nothing from the body is logged. A message is one request body or one response body.

id.description: The caller's own name for one timer, such as <loop id>.<step>.reminder. Unique within one request. Returned unchanged on its answer.

item_id.description: The id of a computed item whose unit is date in the engine output for the case, such as opt_job_end.report.closes.<record id>. A window's ends are its .opens and .closes items.

from_item.description: Start from the date the engine computes for this item on the case sent.

date.description: A date the person typed or confirmed, taken as it is. Never a date the screen worked out.

from_date.description: Start from a date the person gave.

from_today.description: Start from today as the engine reads it: its Clock in the case's time_zone, the same day as the engine output's today.date.

add_business_days.description: Business days: weekends and the federal holidays the engine already counts out (rule calendar.federal_holidays_law) are skipped. The answer names that rule.

add_months.description: Calendar months. A day the target month does not have becomes that month's last day.

setting.description: The id of a row in contracts/product_settings.yaml, such as loop.deadline_lead_days. Its value is the amount and its unit (days, business_days or months) is the kind of offset.

add_setting.description: An amount set by a product setting. A product setting is Duly's own choice, never a rule, and a date from it is a planning date.

add.description: The offset from the base date. Always a whole amount of zero or more; sign gives the direction.

sign.description: 1 counts forward from the base date (a follow-up after a step), -1 counts back from it (a reminder before an obligation date).

cap.description: Optional. The obligation this timer belongs to. The answer is never later than this item's date: a later result is moved back to it, and the answer says capped. A cap item with no date gives no date, never an uncapped one.

date.description: The date, or null when the engine cannot give one; missing then says why. Never a guess.

days_away.description: Whole calendar days from today to date, in the case's time zone; negative when the date has passed. Null exactly when date is null.

missing.description: Present only when date is null. item_not_found and cap_not_found: no computed item of unit date has this id in the engine output for the case. item_has_no_date and cap_has_no_date: the item exists but its value is null, so its question stands. setting_not_found: no product setting has this id. setting_unit_not_a_date_offset: the setting's unit is not days, business_days or months.

capped.description: Optional. True when the result fell after the cap item's date and the cap's date was given instead.

planning.description: Optional, present only when the amount came from a product setting: a planning date, not a rule. As in engine_output.schema.json.

rule_ids.description: Optional. The rules the date rests on: the base and cap items' rules, and calendar.federal_holidays_law for business days.

inputs.description: Optional. The values the date and days_away were computed from, as on the engine output's computed items: the base date, the amount and unit, the sign, the cap date and today.

schedule_answer.description: The date for one request, in the order the requests were sent.

case.description: The case the item ids are read from. The engine computes it as POST /v1/compute does, and reads today in its time_zone.

requests.description: The timers to date. An empty list gives an empty answer.

request.description: The body of POST /v1/schedule, and the argument of engine.schedule.

today.description: Today as the engine read it, the day every days_away is counted from.

dates.description: One answer for each request, in the same order and with the same ids.

response.description: The 200 body of POST /v1/schedule, and the reply of engine.schedule.
